;Armed conflicts and attacks
*Five [[Italian Army|Italian soldiers]] are wounded by a bombing in [[Kirkuk]], [[Iraq]]. Three of the soldiers are seriously injured, two of whom suffer an [[amputate]]d leg, while another an amputated foot. The [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/roadside-blast-iraq-injures-italian-soldiers (Fox News)]
*The [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo]] announces it has "neutralized" the leader of an offshoot of a [[Hutu]] militia, the [[Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda]], in another blow to a "weakened group". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-security/congo-army-kills-leader-of-splinter-hutu-militia-group-idUSKBN1XK0DI (Reuters)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria]]
**[[Turkey]] says a [[car bomb]] near the [[Syria]]n city of [[Tell Abyad]] killed at least eight civilians and injured twenty others. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/at-least-8-killed-in-car-bomb-attack-in-northeast-syria/2019/11/10/627abbaa-03c3-11ea-9118-25d6bd37dfb1_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2019 Hong Kong protests]]
**Protesters vandalize a subway station as violence breaks out across the [[New Territories]] amid anger over a demonstrator's death and the arrest of pro-democracy politicians. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-11-10/violence-spreads-across-hong-kong-new-territories/11691062 (ABC News)]

;Arts and culture
*[[2019 Japanese imperial transition]]
**The new [[Emperor of Japan|Emperor]] [[Naruhito]] and his wife Empress [[Empress Masako|Masako]] take part in a parade in central [[Tokyo]] as tens of thousands of onlookers line the streets in celebration of the [[Enthronement of the Japanese emperor|emperor's enthronement]]. [https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20191110/p2g/00m/0na/027000c (''Mainichi Shimbun'')] [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2019/11/d98e3770aa6f-in-photos-japanese-emperor-naruhitos-enthronement-parade.html (Kyodo News Plus)] [https://apnews.com/e15fd3500daa4587b8b4f3bef63c1090 (Associated Press)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Bolivian protests]], [[Evo Morales government resignation]]
**[[Bolivian President]] [[Evo Morales]] announces new general elections after accusations of fraud. [https://www.dw.com/en/bolivia-evo-morales-calls-for-new-elections-after-oas-audit/a-51190661 (Deutsche Welle)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/10/world/americas/bolivia-election-evo-morales.html (''The New York Times'')]
**Hours after the announcement, Morales resigns from the presidency amid pressure from the [[Armed Forces of Bolivia|military]] and the police in what he deemed a '[[coup d'etat|coup]]'. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-50370013 (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/nov/10/bolivian-president-evo-morales-resigns-after-election-result-dispute (''The Guardian'')]
**The constitutional successors of Morales, [[Vice President of Bolivia|Vice President]] [[Álvaro García Linera]], [[President of the Senate of Bolivia|President of the Senate]] [[Adriana Salvatierra]] and [[President of the Chamber of Deputies of Bolivia|President of the Chamber of Deputies]] Víctor Borda also resign. Mining Minister César Navarro also announces his resignation. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-bolivia-election-salvatierra/bolivian-senate-president-salvatierra-announces-resignation-idUKKBN1XK0NI (Reuters)]
**Vice President of the Senate [[Jeanine Áñez]] becomes the acting president of Bolivia, the [[List of elected and appointed female heads of state and government|first woman]] to ascend to that office. [https://time.com/5726315/bolivia-opposition-leader-jeanine-anez/ (''Time'')]
*[[2019 Romanian presidential election]]
**People in [[Romania]] cast their votes in the country's latest presidential election. [https://www.dw.com/en/romania-iohannis-tipped-for-runoff-before-second-term-as-president/a-51187403 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[Israel–Jordan peace treaty]]
**Israel returns the territory of the "[[Island of Peace]]" to Jordan. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/gate-closes-at-isle-of-peace-park-as-border-lands-to-return-to-jordan (''The Times of Israel'')] 
*[[November 2019 Spanish general election]]
**Citizens of [[Spain]] head to the polls for the second general election within a year. [https://www.dw.com/en/spain-returns-to-the-polls-to-break-political-deadlock/a-51155618 (Deutsche Welle)] 
**The [[Spanish Socialist Worker's Party|PSOE]], headed by incumbent [[Prime Minister of Spain|Prime Minister]] [[Pedro Sánchez]], wins the election but loses 3 seats and its absolute majority in the [[Senate of Spain|Senate]]. Political deadlock remains. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/ng-interactive/2019/nov/10/spanish-general-election-2019-live-results (''The Guardian'')]
**Far-right [[Vox (political party)|Vox]] gains 28 seats and raises from fifth to the third national force. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-50367870 (BBC News)]
**The center-right [[Citizens (Spanish political party)|Citizens]], the third national force going into the elections, goes from 57 seats in Congress to just 10, the biggest seat loss in the election. [[Albert Rivera]] quits as Citizens' leader as a result. [https://elpais.com/elpais/2019/11/11/inenglish/1573467972_489207.html (''El País'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2019/11/10/world/europe/ap-eu-spain-election-the-latest.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[2019 Chilean protests]]
**An American [[white supremacist]] shoots a protester in [[Viña del Mar|Reñaca]]. Before being detained by the police, he uploads a video to YouTube confessing the attack, claiming to have fired in [[self-defense]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2019/11/11/john-cobin-chile-shooting-protesters-video/ (''The Washington Post'')]
**Interior Minister {{ill|Gonzalo Blumel|es}} announces the government will propose the creation of a new [[2022 proposed Political Constitution of the Republic of Chile|constitution]] through the existing [[National Congress of Chile|Congress]] instead of a [[constituent assembly]] as requested by the protesters. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-11-11/chile-s-government-to-propose-mechanism-for-a-new-constitution (Bloomberg News)]

;Sports
*[[2019 MLS Cup Playoffs]]
**The [[Seattle Sounders FC]] defeat [[Toronto FC]] 3–1 at [[CenturyLink Field]] to win their second MLS Cup. [https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2019/11/10/seattle-sounders-are-2019-mls-cup-champions-rave-green-win-second-mls-title (Major League Soccer)]
